## Step 1: A write-ahead log is a record of all changes made to the database.
The database maintains a log of all changes made to the data, including insertions, deletions, and updates. This log is typically stored in a separate location from the main database files.

## Step 2: When a transaction is committed, the changes are recorded in the log.
Before the changes are written to the main database files, the transaction is recorded in the log. This ensures that if a crash occurs before the changes are written to the database, the log can be used to recover the changes.

## Step 3: After a crash, the database can use the log to recover changes.
In the event of a crash, the database can read the log and apply the changes recorded in it to the main database files. This allows the database to recover the data that was lost due to the crash.

## Step 4: The database can also use the log to detect inconsistencies.
By checking the log against the main database files, the database can detect any inconsistencies that may have occurred due to the crash. This allows the database to take corrective action to restore data integrity.
